period_reason: Two complete weeks aligned with the latest Webmaster search data used in organic-yandex-2026-10-07.json; not the original month range.
access_resolution: User opened the counter in the Codex in-app browser under OFFICE-9102. This session has report access; the earlier Chrome session returned 403.

crm_presentation_lead_received.interpretation: This is a manual offline import goal according to the existing export workflow. No data does not by itself mean delivery failed.

observations: Five favorite goal reaches represent one form success, three phone clicks and one email click, not five unique leads.
The server recorded 18 sent QA submissions, two QA submissions without receipts and one sent submission without QA markers in this period.
The one submission without QA markers is present in Presentation with a site tag and no QA tag or test title. It is currently closed and not realized; delivery is not a sale.

The unique non-QA submission and the organic success event share the October 2 date and AUSN landing page. This supports their correspondence, but no visitor identifier was exported to assert an exact ClientID match.
One organic visit has a form failure event; an event alone does not identify an HTTP error or prove a currently failing form.
Organic acquisition volume is small: 12 Yandex-attributed visits in fourteen days. Behavioral figures are based on a very small sample.
limitations: Last significant cross-device attribution can include return visits, so Webmaster clicks and Metrika visits are not interchangeable.
Phone/email clicks are not confirmed calls or qualified inquiries.
QA filtering uses documented field/tag rules and does not prove every unmarked record is a qualified customer.
The receipt source referrer is the website itself; the Yandex attribution is observed in Metrika.
The original traffic report shows 1690 visits; the sources report shows 1685 with undefined sources disabled. The five-visit difference was not assigned to a source.
